💡 Key Takeaways

  • Leeds United have reportedly moved towards agreeing a contract extension for midfielder Ao Tanaka.
  • The Japan international has been a key part of Daniel Farke's side this season and started as the Whites smashed Chelsea by a 4-1 scoreline at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League last weekend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 09:57.

Leeds United have reportedly moved towards agreeing a contract extension for midfielder Ao Tanaka.

The Japan international has been a key part of Daniel Farke's side this season and started as the Whites smashed Chelsea by a 4-1 scoreline at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League last weekend.

Leading the line for the visitors in West London, Dominic-Calvert-Lewin is also supposedly on the verge of putting pen to paper on fresh terms at Elland Road, with Leeds closing in on the striker's renewed signature.

Losing just two matches in the top flight so far this term, Leeds are currently occupying seventh position in the Premier League standings, with the Yorkshire giants targeting European qualification.

Aiming to record three straight league wins for the first time this campaign, Farke's side will be the heavy favourites on Saturday afternoon, when they welcome former Championship foes Coventry City to Elland Road.

According to Sky Sports News, Leeds are moving decisively ahead of a busy festive period on the pitch, with the European hopefuls aiming to resolve the long-term futures of Calvert-Lewin and Tanaka.

The report states that the Whites are closing in on a contract extension for Japanese midfielder Tanaka, whose current deal at Elland Road expires at the conclusion of the 2027-28 domestic cycle.

It is understood that Farke's side have offered the ex-Fortuna Dusseldorf man an extra 12 months of contract security, meaning that he is set to be committed to the cause until June 2029.

At the beginning of the calendar year, there was a real question mark over whether Tanaka had a future in the first-team ranks of Leeds, who were comfortably avoiding a relegation battle without the 28-year-old in their starting XI.

However, the engine-room enforcer has since fought his way back to the front of the prepares for the Whites, with the midfielder starting nine of the club's 11 Premier League fixtures in 2026-27 so far.

Given the positive trajectory of Leeds over the past few years, it is no surprise that contract extensions are the talk of the town at the moment, with the club's hierarchy keen to tie their best assets down.

On the pitch, Tanaka and Calvert-Lewin have been key to the first-team progression at Elland Road, with the Whites looking set to establish themselves as a Premier League regular over the coming years.

Bringing Leeds back up from the Championship in 2025, head coach Farke is also in line for a newly introduced contract, with the German tactician certainly deserving of such a reward in the near future.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Brighton and Hove Albion will begin consulting supporters and stakeholders on plans to build Europe's first purpose-built women's football stadium in the coming weeks.
  • Chief executive and deputy chairman Paul Barber confirmed the next stage in his programme notes ahead of Thursday night's Conference League fixture with Craiova.
  • Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Brighton and Hove Albion will begin consulting supporters and stakeholders on plans to build Europe's first purpose-built women's football stadium in the coming weeks.

Chief executive and deputy chairman Paul Barber confirmed the next stage in his programme notes ahead of Thursday night's Conference League fixture with Craiova. Barber stated a public consultation event will take place in the Terrace at the Amex Stadium on December 9.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Barber said: "In the coming weeks we will begin consulting with supporters and stakeholders on our intends for the first purpose-built stadium in Europe and home for Brighton and Hove Albion Women, with an event planned for December 9 from 2-8pm at the Terrace at the Amex.

"It's a hugely key project, not only for our club but for the future of the women's game across Sussex, and we will share more details of the event very soon.".

The announcement represents a step towards delivering a permanent home for Albion Women, with the club having formally unveiled its stadium proposals in April.

The proposed 10,000-capacity ground will be built at Bennett's Field, adjacent to the American Express Stadium, and connected to the Amex by a new bridge walkway.

Brighton hope to open the stadium in time for the 2030-31 season, subject to planning permission from Brighton and Hove City Council and Lewes District Council.

The estimated cost of the project is between £75m and £80m, with owner Tony Bloom backing the significant investment.

The stadium is being designed specifically around the needs of female players and supporters, with bespoke changing rooms, recovery facilities and a matchday experience aimed at families and first-time visitors.

Brighton currently play the majority of their Women's Super League home fixtures at Crawley Town's Broadfield Stadium, although selected matches have been staged at the Amex.

The new development would provide the women's team with a permanent base in the city and form a major part of the club's long-term ambitions to grow women's and girls' football across Sussex.

THE BREAKDOWN: The real reasons why Enzo Maresca's Man City can't stop losing - from anonymous Enzo Fernandez abandoning Elliot Anderson, to the fatal flaws in Italian's set-up that are being brutally exposed

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1735 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 07:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 05:23 EST, 26 November 2026.
  • Enzo Maresca may look like Pep Guardiola, may have learned his craft under his Manchester City predecessor, but his quest to follow in his mentor’s footsteps has all gone a bit flat.
  • Seven successive Premier League wins to start his City reign, a record for a fresh manager in the competition, breaking one jointly-held by Guardiola, gave the impression that this might be a smooth passing of the torch after all.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 07:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 05:23 EST, 26 November 2026.

Diet Pep is losing his fizz. Enzo Maresca may look like Pep Guardiola, may have learned his craft under his Manchester City predecessor, but his quest to follow in his mentor’s footsteps has all gone a bit flat.

Seven successive Premier League wins to start his City reign, a record for a fresh manager in the competition, breaking one jointly-held by Guardiola, gave the impression that this might be a smooth passing of the torch after all.

Three months in, and three defeats on the spin that left them six points behind Arsenal have made it clear that something is not clicking for Maresca.

Is the uncertainty around the potential punishment following that guilty verdict taking its toll? Is Maresca just suffering from his usual late autumn dips? He suffered similar tricky periods around late October and early November at Leicester and his first season at Chelsea too.

Or is there something at the heart of his side, of his system, that’s finally being exposed?

Enzo Maresca's Man City have slumped to three straight Premier League defeats after a promising start to the season.

It has been revealed that guardiola’s City was all about control. Keep the ball, dominate the pitch, play the game at your pace, on your terms.

Sources indicate that maresca’s City, regardless of how well they started the season, has been about anything but. It has been about triumph amid chaos, about moments of magic more than the overarching method.

Sources indicate that without that control, City’s defensive issues have been laid bare. The 13 goals they have let in after 10 games is their most at this stage since 2008. They haven’t kept a clean sheet in their last eight matches in all competitions. That's a drought longer than at any point under Guardiola.

Their biggest problem over City's three successive Premier League defeats is just how susceptible they have been to counter attacks.

Only Newcastle have faced more shots this season following ‘fast breaks’ – data giants Opta's term for counter attacks – than City’s 17, and 11 of those have come in the last three games: six against Nottingham Forest, two of which led to goals, three against Brighton and another two against Aston Villa.

Maresca’s side are being more profligate in possession, too. Over the first seven games of the season, they lost the ball 120 times a game on average – one of the best figures in the division. Since then, it’s closer to 140.

City have been wasteful in possession and regularly overrun on the counter, with Elliot Anderson (centre) too often left isolated in midfield.

ANDERSON CAN'T DO IT ALL ON HIS OWN.

Sources indicate that many of these problems have their roots in Maresca's serious problems in midfield. Rodri, the best holding midfielder of his generation, was always going to be hard to replace but Maresca appears to be expecting Elliot Anderson to do it all on his own.

Recent findings suggest that anderson is at his best when he’s free to get up and down the pitch, box to box, using his physicality not just in winning the ball back but progressing it. No midfielder played more passes into the final third last season than Anderson at Forest. At one stage of the campaign, he had played more progressive passes than any other player across Europe’s top five leagues.

And yet Maresca is forcing Anderson to play as the sitter while his golden boy Enzo Fernandez, whom he pushed City to sign in the summer for £125million, is roaming free and high up the pitch.

Maresca likes his teams to build up in a 3-1-6 shape, which sees Fernandez push up as an extra attacking midfielder, and leaves Anderson manning the fort alone.

When City lose the ball, though, it leaves them wide open.

Sources indicate that this is the opening goal City conceded against Forest. Josko Gvardiol wants to play the ball inside but has only red shirts and empty green space ahead of him. Anderson is the only man free, but even he is too high and has a Forest player ready to cut off the pass. Eventually, Gvardiol gets robbed and Forest score.

A lack of options for Josko Gvardiol (left) led to Forest's opener against City. Enzo Fernandez (circled) was caught high up the pitch, way ahead of the deeper Anderson (also circled).

Here’s another moment in the defeat by Brighton.

The Seagulls break forward on the flank and Anderson races over to close the ball down. Fernandez is, you guessed it, high up the pitch.

City have no midfield cover to stop the ball inside, Abdukodir Khusanov gets drawn in and leaves loads of space in behind for Yasin Ayari to exploit and cross to Maxim De Cuyper for a great chance.

The lack of protection offered by Anderson and especially the more advanced Fernandez was again on show against Brighton, who were able to exploit the acres of space left in midfield.

According to recent reports, fernandez is doing what Maresca wants, but it’s not working. Maresca needs more from him, especially when Anderson’s instincts are to press and harass and bully, which can leave gaps when he does not yet read the game as comprehensively as Rodri.

Recent findings suggest that anderson sits in the top five for ball recoveries among midfielders to have played 500 minutes this season. Fernandez is in the bottom five. That figure becomes even more alarming when you consider Anderson has created more chances from open play than Fernandez, too.

Ayyoub Bouaddi highlighted at the World Cup that he had the most similar profile to Rodri. It might be time for Maresca to put some faith in him.

Maresca has always wanted his goalkeeper to be an 11th outfielder. In his one season at Leicester, Mads Hermansen played more passes than any goalkeeper in Championship history. During his time at Chelsea, there was a shaky moment in a draw with Arsenal when loud groans greeted a misplaced pass from Robert Sanchez.

‘I am the guy who asks Robert to do that,’ remarked Maresca after that game. ‘The moment he stops doing that, he is not going to play.’.

In a recent development, donnarumma, though, for all his (usually) excellent shot-stopping, is anything but a ball-playing goalkeeper. The ball rolled under his foot from a simple back pass against Coventry and so nearly crept over the line. He gifted France an early lead while on international duty with Italy when he passed the ball straight to Michael Olise.

Only two keepers made more errors leading to shots than Donnarumma across the course of last season, with many of those being with his feet, like when he gifted Kai Havertz an equaliser in City's victory over Arsenal in April.

Gianluigi Donnarumma has never been good with his feet - now his excellent shot-stopping has taken a dip too.

The Italian should have easily dealt with Nicolas Jackson's second goal in City's 2-1 loss at Aston Villa.

The decision to let James Trafford leave in the summer, especially with Guardiola’s impending departure and a manager like Maresca coming in, is looking ever more misguided.

Sources indicate that trafford is not immune to mistakes either, of course. He erred badly when trying to play out from the back for City against Spurs last season and made an almost identical howler for Leeds at Bournemouth in October. But he is still far more confident at playing out from the back than Donnarumma.

The double blow for Maresca is that the trade-off with Donnarumma – where he makes up for his weakness with the ball at his feet by making saves that other keepers can’t make – is no longer paying off either.

Nicolas Jackson’s shot squirmed straight through him to hand Villa victory and condemn City to their first defeat of the season.

When you are coughing up chances as frequently as City are, Maresca needs his keeper to be on top form.

Do you know who is keeping the ball out of his net? James Trafford. He boasts the highest save percentage of any goalkeeper in the top flight, keeping out 81 per cent of the shots on target coming his way. Donnarumma is 15th, on less than 66 per cent.

It has been revealed that according to Opta’s expected data, Trafford has also prevented more than four goals that he should have conceded from the quality of the shots he’s faced. Again, he’s the best in the Premier League. Donnarumma is middle of the pack.

It has been revealed that ‘At the moment, I’m not thinking about the goalkeeping situation,’ said Maresca recently. Without Trafford there and just 34-year-old Geronimo Rulli as back-up, he doesn’t really have a choice but to persist with Donnarumma and hope he improves.

When the goals stop flowing for Erling Haaland, City can't mask all their other problems.

So used are we now to seeing the Norwegian on the scoresheet, having notched nine in City’s opening eight matches, that when he goes just two games without a goal it feels as if he’s on a barren spell.

The matter, though, is less down to Haaland and more that City’s build-up in recent weeks is struggling to get him into the game.

Industry observers note that city are finding it more difficult to get Haaland on the ball. His touches per game are falling steadily but, crucially, so are the quality of the chances his team-mates are creating for him.

Recent findings suggest that haaland had more than one Opta-defined 'big chance' in five of City’s opening seven games. He’s had just one come his way in each of their three defeats.

His expected goals (xG) tally is dropping too. Across City’s winning streak, Haaland’s average xG per match was 0.81. Only once, against Liverpool, did it drop below 0.5.

Over the three defeats, it’s just 0.45 and has not once gone above 0.5.

Antoine Semenyo missing the last three games through injury has not helped, especially when teams now try to pack the middle of the pitch and force City wide.

Haaland will come good, he always does, but City need to start serving him again if Maresca wants to get through this tricky spell and stop the vultures from circling.

Celtic are in Europa League action on Thursday night when they travel to Portugal to face second-tier side Torreense.

The game will mark the first time in history that the Hoops have contested a European fixture against a team who are not competing in the top flight of their domestic league.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Torreense qualified for the Europa League after a fairytale cup success last season, defying the odds to beat Sporting Lisbon in the final of the Portuguese Cup to claim the first major trophy in their 109-year existence.

They failed to secure promotion, however, losing 2-0 on aggregate to Casa Pia in the promotion/relegation play-off, meaning they remained in Liga Portugal 2 for the 2026/27 campaign, where they current sit 13th in the table.

Celtic put their first Europa League points on the board at the fourth attempt with a 3-2 win over Besiktas on November 5 following three consecutive defeats by Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo.

Martin O’Neill’s side sit 32nd in the 36-team league with four games to play as they bid to climb into the top 24 and become the first side to qualify for the knockout stages after losing their opening three league phase matches.

Torreense are in a healthier 19th position having collected six points from their opening four games with victories over Lillestrom and Ararat-Armenia mixed with defeats to Sunderland and Ferencvaros.

Recent findings suggest that the Europa League match between Torreense and Celtic will take place on Thursday, November 26, 2026 at the Dr. Magalhães Pessoa Stadium in Leiria. The venue is 60 miles away from Torreense’s actual home in Torres Vedras, as their own stadium only has 2,500 seats and does not meet Uefa requirements. Kick-off is 8pm.

The match will be shown live on TNT Sports 3 with coverage starting at 7.45pm, following on from Hearts v Monaco on the same channel.

Fans can stream the match live via HBO Max or Amazon Prime Video with a TNT Sports subscription.

Free highlights will be posted on the TNT Sports Football YouTube channel shortly after full-time.

Celtic have added Jota to their Europa League squad in place of the injured Mika Baur. The Portuguese winger was initially left out as he fought his way back from a serious knee injury. But he could now feature in his homeland against Torreense after continuing his comeback with a start in Saturday’s 4-1 win over St Mirren. Baur was recently ruled out for up to 10 weeks with ankle ligament damage.

Benjamin Nygren is nursing a heel problem while Alistair Johnston remains sidelined by a hamstring injury.

Torreense are missing suspended Jorge Aguirre following his red card in the 3-2 win over Aararat-Armenia and the injured Adama Baradji.

An all-Dutch officiating team will take charge of the match. Allard Lindhout is the on-field referee and he will be joined on the pitch by assistant referees Johan Balder and Murat Kucukerbir, while Jannick van der Laan serves as the fourth official. Pol van Boekel has been assigned as the Video Assistant Referee (VAR) with Dennis Johan Higler acting as the Assistant Video Assistant Referee (AVAR).

Torreense 4/1, Draw 7/2, Celtic 4/6 - via oddschecker.com.

Jason Steele will make his first Conference League start of the season against Craiova.

The Brighton goalkeeper steps up against the Romanians as regular No 1 Bart Verbruggen drops to the bench.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Steele, 36, has previously featured twice this campaign with both outings in the Carabao Cup at Manchester United and then Manchester City, where Brighton lost on penalties.

Verbruggen conceded five goals during the international break as The Netherlands were walloped by Germany and then conceded twice in last Sunday's 2-0 defeat at Hull.

Head coach Fabian Hurzeler previously remarked that Steele will feature in the Conference League and the German may have felt now was the right time to give Verbruggen a rest - especially as Newcastle at the Amex Stadium this Sunday for a Premier League.

Recent findings suggest that steele featured five times for Brighton in the Europa League in 2023-24 under previous boss Roberto De Zerbi. His last European outing was the 4-0 loss at Roma in March 2024.

In a recent development, elsewhere, Turkey international Ferdi Kadioglu will start at right back in place of Costinha, who was sent off at Hull. Michael Svoboda and Pascal Struijk - his first start in six weeks - will form the central defensive partnership as Lewis Dunk and Luka Vuskovic put their feet up on the bench. It looks as though Maxim De Cuyper will slot in at left back.

Pascal Gross maintains his proud record of starting every match this season and the 35-year-old will be joined in central midfield by impressive young Spaniard Chema Andres.

Matt O’Riley is handed a rare start on the right flank with Ibrahim Osman given another chance to shine on the left. Jack Hinshelwood will operate in the No 10 role behind Greek striker Charalampos Kostoulas.

Kostoulas was benched at Hull as he missed training the day before due to personal reasons.

Femi Azeez - Brighton’s summer arrival from Millwall - is included in a matchday squad for the first time and is expected to make his full debut at some stage.

Brighton XI: Steele; Kadioglu, Svoboda, Struijk, De Cuyper; Gross, Chema; O'Riley, Hinshelwood, Osman; Kostoulas. Substitutes: Verbruggen, McGill, Dunk, Georginio, Promise, Costinha, Ayari, Azeez, Vuskovic, Nti, Ibrahim.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 26 Nov 2026 10:16.

Former Manchester United star Gordon Strachan - speaking exclusively to Sports Mole - has urged the Red Devils to sign a £62.8m midfielder to help correct their "phenomenal" transfer mistakes.

Latest Man Utd manager Mauricio Pochettino remains winless since replacing Michael Carrick following Wednesday's infuriating 2-2 draw with Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League, in which the Red Devils fell behind, took the lead and were then pegged back in Portugal.

The four-goal stalemate marked the seventh game in a row that Man United had conceded at least two goals, and once again, the Red Devils' open midfield was exposed.

The pairing of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo did not cover themselves in glory against Liverpool or Sporting, and the former is now suspended for RB Leipzig in December after being sent off towards the end of Wednesday's game.

Andrey Santos has also not yet had the desired impact since joining from Chelsea, while fellow 22-year-old Carlos Baleba has played just 397 minutes across seven appearances due to injury problems.

Speaking to Sports Mole via William Hill betting site, Strachan - who scored 36 goals in 198 games for Man United - has told the Red Devils hierarchy to make a move for Crystal Palace lynchpin Adam Wharton to help offset the "phenomenal" amount of money the club has wasted on under-performing players.

"Adam Wharton is one of my picks," Strachan said. "Elliot Anderson was also another one they should have gone for. Tielemans has been doing well in the Premier League for nearly 10 years, so they're buying somebody who's at the latter stage of his career. I might be wrong, I hope I'm wrong, and hopefully, he’s got another five or six years in him.

Recent findings suggest that "And I've got to say, the world of football in England is full of the top teams, especially Chelsea, Spurs, bringing in players who sign for £40m, £50m, you go, who is he? There's just so many players like this now.

"You see some of these players, and you go, what has he done to deserve a £45m fee? Baleba, Santos, you’re picking up people for massive fees, who have no reputation.

"Who's been brave here? Is this just a kind of cosy midfield? You could go back to Mason Mount for £40m - who actually signed this off to pay this amount of money for players?

"It’s just beyond belief the money that Man United have wasted. It's phenomenal. And that's from the recruitment not doing their work properly.

Sources indicate that "They've got to start saying, what is my plan for the next 10 years at Man United? And how do we go about this? Arsenal were a bit like that five or six years ago. It wasn't anywhere near as bad a situation as Man United, but they stuck to their plan, and it paid off.".

Data from the 2026-27 season does not paint Wharton in the most positive light compared to his Man United peers, given Crystal Palace's atrocious start to the campaign.

Indeed, the England international only leads Baleba, Tielemans, Santos and Mainoo on games played, crosses per 90 and accurate crosses per 90, while also winning the fewest duels and registering the lowest percentage of successful passes.

However, Wharton has committed the fewest fouls per 90 minutes of the quintet, and he has been dispossessed on the second-fewest occasions per 90 minutes, only behind Santos.

Thanks to Crystal Palace's perilous position in the Premier League table - Thomas Frank's men sit bottom of the rankings with just seven points from nine games - interested parties could pick up Wharton for a discount if the Eagles are relegated to the Championship.

The 22-year-old is valued at €75m (£62.8m) by Transfermarkt and has three years left on his Palace contract, but Man United may have to fend off competition from Liverpool and Chelsea to land him in 2027.

Gordon Strachan was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of William Hill Football Odds.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scottish football chiefs have extended the consultation period for its prepares to encourage the selection of more youngsters “with the intention of a comprehensive proposal within the first quarter of 2027” amid concerns from some major clubs.

The Scottish Football Association invited all 42 league clubs to a summit at St Andrews in early September, where they unveiled a package of proposals aimed at securing the future of the sport in Scotland.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The SFA wants a minimum of two Scottish under-21 players to be selected by each team in a Scottish Cup tie and for two Scottish under-21 players to be picked by each team in the Premier Sports Cup, starting from the 2027/28 campaign.

From next season as well, the SFA has also suggested under-21 players be on the pitch for an average of 60 minutes per game, across the season, in the Premiership, equating to six per cent of available minutes.

Led by recently-appointed chief football officer Craig Mulholland, the SFA had hoped to put some of their aims to a vote at the Scottish Professional Football League annual general meeting this month. With a downward trajectory of young Scottish players being selected in the Premiership over the past ten years, Mulholland stated in September that “we need to act now, otherwise we could end up finding ourselves in a crisis at some point in the future”.

The fear is that Scotland risks falling behind similarly-sized nations and will fail to qualify for major tournaments, while Premiership clubs were told by external firm Twenty First Group that they are leaving £40 million on the table in potential revenue by not placing more faith in academy players.

Nevertheless, The Scotsman understands that some of the SFA’s proposals have been met with scepticism from clubs across the leagues and the governing body has extended the consultation period “into the New Year” to continue dialogue on the best way forward.

A statement from the Scottish Football Association read: “The Scottish FA has been encouraged by the productive dialogue with clubs regarding proposals to harness opportunities for young homegrown talent.

“The most recent discussions have spawned a range of additional potential innovations that all parties agree will require further consultation in order to present a consolidated package of recommendations to an SPFL member vote.

“The passion we all have for Scottish football has been demonstrated by the public debate sparked since the all-club meeting in St Andrews, when the reality of our domestic game’s standing in respect of playing time for under-21 players compared to the rest of Europe was made clear.

“We will continue to engage in dialogue with the aim of delivering a proposal that will achieve the stated objective of improving opportunities for young homegrown players to fulfil their potential at the top end of the Scottish professional game.

“It is an objective everyone benefits from: players, clubs, supporters and Scotland national teams.

“We have therefore agreed that the consultation process will continue into the New Year with the intention of a comprehensive proposal going to SPFL members within the first quarter of 2027, in time for the start of William Hill SPFL season 2027-28.

“The Scottish FA General Meeting to vote on the complementary Scottish Gas Men’s Scottish Cup proposals will now follow a similar timetable.

“Given the implications for our game, and our young talent, it is imperative that we take the necessary time to get those proposals right.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Last night, a report was published comparing the financials of AC Milan, Juventus and Inter and the findings are very interesting.

It has been revealed that the massive three bring a lot of attention to Italy and their footballing ecosystem, but that’s not all. Indeed, all three bring in vast amounts of money and have done so for years, which has helped them establish this dominance. However, their records last season show that a change could be on the way.

As Gazzetta dello Sport writes, via Calciomercato.com, Inter recorded the highest revenue last season of €518 million, Juventus slotted in with €474.4m and then the Rossoneri finished ‘last’ with a revenue of €464.6m.

However, the profits – about that – of all three clubs didn’t line up in the same order. Inter recorded a €23m loss, then it was Milan with a €24m loss – largely helped by the summer signings – and Juventus finished last with a €66m loss.

Industry observers note that considering the Nerazzurri’s sporting successes in recent years, it makes sense why revenues are considerably higher, especially when looking at their Champions League records. For example, not being in Europe cost the Diavolo €54m between 2024/25 and 2025/26.

In terms of squad cost, the Biaconeri were uncontested at the top, with a wage of €210m per season. Inter finished just below with €204m per season, whilst the Rossoneri ‘only’ spent €146m. Of course, this is still lucrative.

All in all, the foundations laid at Casa Milan are looking strong and if they can become more successful, their revenues could rocket up.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that eight goals at Dens Park is one thing. Going toe-to-toe with French aristocrats and being beaten, cruelly, at the death is quite another. Hearts’ growing reputation as the great entertainers was nevertheless burnished here in thrilling fashion.

The price the Hearts fans might have to pay for such swashbuckling play was also demonstrated. Defensive fragility was all too apparent, including at the end when substitute Mamadou Coulibaly brushed off a challenge in midfield and threaded the ball through for Folarin Balogun to score his second and the night’s decisive goal. We were already into the final minute of the four added on at the end of a quite breathless European tie.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Mon Dieu! What a match. AS Monaco won’t forget this trip to Scotland, and a vibrant Tynecastle, in a hurry. As for the hosts, they remain just about alive in the Conference League.

The point they were deprived in heartbreaking fashion would have made such a difference. As good as Monaco are, it wasn’t as if Hearts were undone by a moment of genius, which makes it harder to bear. The hosts also had chances to score their own third goal and were angered when referee Daniel Schlager waved away penalty appeals when substitute Josh McPake ended up in a heap after Jordan Teze’s challenge.

Recent findings suggest that perhaps the home supporters will simply have to put up with see-sawing emotions in a season that’s already shaping up to be one of the craziest in the club’s history. Perhaps defensive slackness, although costly, must simply be endured if goals continue to flow at the other end, especially ones as sensational as Hearts fans were treated to here. Drop them off in the Louvre on your way home, Monaco.

Jordi Altena’s opener was declared a “potential” goal of the season by the always judicious Tynecastle Tannoy announcer. Just as well because a better one was just around the corner. Sabah Kerjota’s curler on the stroke of half time was an immaculate finish that Lukas Hradecky, the experienced keeper, just had to stand rooted to his spot and admire.

Industry observers note that altena’s strike was not quite in the same unsavable part of the goal but it was still breathtaking in its execution. Kerjota, the little Albanian livewire, also played a part in it. His free-kick looked to be going in until Hradecky pushed the ball against the post. Claudio Braga made sure the ball was recycled and played it back to Kerjota, who passed it inside to Altena. The Dutchman is fast becoming a Tynecastle favourite. No wonder when he can strike a ball like this. Hradecky was left flapping at the air beneath his bar.

Since going 5-0 down to Falkirk after 47 minutes earlier this month at Tynecastle, Hearts had scored 10 unanswered goals. This was the 11th. The response was always coming. This was AS Monaco after all. They might be struggling right now in Ligue 1 but how can they be they be written off? The team remains packed full of talent. This was not the shadow side Hearts might have hoped to face. Eric Dier, the England international, was present and correct as was former Arsenal player – and Donald Trump’s friend - Balogun.

Recent findings suggest that monaco were the ones raising a quizzical French eyebrow at the home team sheet. Due to much publicised injury problems and lack of adequate club-trained academy players, Hearts couldn’t even fill the bench.

Matthew Gillies stepped in for his first senior start in midfield. Unless Monaco were familiar with Stenhousemuir's opening matches of this season, the talented 19-year-old might have been something of a mystery to them. The same applies to Finlay Pollock, who is something of a mystery to Hearts fans as well.

According to recent reports, pollock came on towards the end for his first Hearts appearance since 2024. The 22-year-old has been out on loan at East Fife and Raith Rovers in between times. He was given the last nine minutes in place of a drained Kerjota. The whole team, including substitutes, looked shattered at the end but they had contributed to a game that will live long in the memory. There was the drama of an overturned penalty for Hearts in the second half after an alleged handball by substitute Mathys Detourbet as well as the sight of Beau Reus galloping up field for a corner in the final seconds.

The visitors’ first goal of the night saw Balogun do the necessary – and no more - from the penalty spot after Stuart Findlay had clipped the heels of the dangerous Matthis Abline.

There was some dismay among home fans about Reus’ lack of movement. Balogun’s penalty lacked conviction and certainly wasn’t placed in the corner. Far from it. Nevertheless, it brought Monaco level. The French side took heart although they didn’t have it all their own way. Abline was booked for a foul on Laurent Mendy as Hearts forced the visitors into sometimes desperate measures.

Monaco did though take the lead for the first time in the night five minutes before half time after Edan Diop took advantage of a slack ball from Altena following a throw-in. After playing a one-two with Balogun, he slipped the ball beyond Reus.

In a recent development, gillies was showing his worth in midfield. He might have had a goal to tell his pals about had Pierre Landry Kabore not taken the ball off his foot as he was preparing to unleash a shot from the edge of the box. Kabore, following his brace against Dundee, was in frisky form but often got a little too excited and forgot the basics, such as avoiding running into teammates.

Gillies was withdrawn at half time for Blair Spittal, back from injury and desperate to play a part. He also took the captain’s armband from McCart and helped drive Hearts on. Sadly, his and others’ efforts were in vain on an agonising night for the hosts.

Bournemouth vs. Celta Vigo: How the Cherries could equal Chelsea, Leeds feat with Europa League victory

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 10:27.
  • Bournemouth have prepared for their Europa League clash at Celta Vigo in the knowledge that they could smash even more history.
  • Marco Rose's side won just two of their opening eight competitive matches of the 2026-27 season, hinting that there could be a period of struggle following Andoni Iraola's departure to Liverpool.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 10:27.

Bournemouth have prepared for their Europa League clash at Celta Vigo in the knowledge that they could smash even more history.

Marco Rose's side won just two of their opening eight competitive matches of the 2026-27 season, hinting that there could be a period of struggle following Andoni Iraola's departure to Liverpool.

However, with the Cherries set for a Celta Vigo challenge on Thursday night, it is clear that the Dean Court club are thriving, with the visitors to Spain sitting in fifth position in the Premier League standings.

A star of the current positive form, Evanilson has truly unveiled himself as an elite top-flight striker, netting seven goals and providing two assists in his past eight appearances, scoring in five consecutive league fixtures.

What makes Bournemouth's run even more impressive is that last season's star man Junior Kroupi has barely started a competitive match so far after recovering from a broken leg sustained over the summer.

Starting with a 3-0 Europa League success over Austrian side Sturm Graz on October 15, Bournemouth have recorded nine straight victories in all competitions across the Premier League, EFL Cup and European action.

That winning streak is the longest since the Cherries became a Football League club at the beginning of the 1923-24 season, showcasing how impressively the South Coast team are performing at the moment.

However, there are still more records to be achieved over the coming weeks, with Bournemouth aiming to become only the eighth team to record 10 straight competitive victories whilst playing in the Premier League.

Winning the Premier League during the 2016-17 campaign under Antonio Conte, Chelsea managed 10 wins in a row in all competitions, with that particular streak running from October 2016 until Newly introduced Year's Eve 2016.

Leeds are the other club to post that exact number of wins in succession, with the Elland Road side completing the feat between August and October during the 1999-00 Premier League term.

The dominant force in English domestic football during the late 2010s and early 2020s, Manchester City are unsurprisingly the club with the most consecutive competitive wins as a Premier League side.

Under the expert stewardship of Pep Guardiola, the title-winning Citizens won 21 straight matches between December 2020 and March 2021, destroying Arsenal's previous record of 13 games in succession.

To match Man City's record, Bournemouth would need to secure victory in Spain on Thursday before winning every single match up to and including the trip to Brighton & Hove Albion on January 5.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The parish council remarked it has been ‘open and transparent’ throughout the process of ‘exploring options for the future of the Pulborough Sports & Social Club building.

It remarked the project ‘remains at an early stage’, and ‘no final decisions have been made’ regarding the detailed design or layout of any replacement facility.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The club's members say the building is about far more than somewhere to have a drink after a match – it is a place where children make friends, parents get to know one another and volunteers help keep village football going.

Matt Parry, who has been involved with Pulborough football for around 30 years as a player and now as a parent and youth coach, remarked the club had become an vital part of family life.

He remarked the youth section had grown to six teams, with players competing in local leagues and cups against clubs from much larger towns.

Matt said the club tried to keep costs down so that children could take part without financial barriers, adding that friendships formed through football often extended beyond the pitch.

After matches, parents and players regularly head into the clubhouse, while events bring the different age groups together.

Recent findings suggest that A special family fun day last weekend celebrated 128 years of the youth football club. Matt stated parents came into the building after the matches to socialise and take part in a fundraising raffle.

“We would not have been able to do that without the building at all,” he remarked.

Tom Hayes, who helped establish the club's youth football provision, also stressed the importance of the social club's support.

The youth section began with just four players and has since grown to six teams. Tom mentioned the social club had helped from the outset, providing equipment and supporting the teams with kit sponsorship and presentation events.

He believes losing the facilities would mean losing an important part of the experience for children and their families, particularly those who value having an affordable place to meet after playing.

Natalie Smiley, who has been the football club secretary for around 17 years and also chairs the social club, said the two organisations were closely connected.

She warned: “If the social club goes, the football club will go with it.”.

Natalie noted the club had expanded considerably during her time involved, with six youth teams now playing alongside the men's side.

According to recent reports, she said the work was carried out by volunteers, who gave up their own time to organise matches, prepare pitches and keep the club running. The social club also provides a base for other activities, including darts, pool and snooker.

According to recent reports, the family day on Sunday, November 22, brought teams, families and supporters together. Natalie estimated that more than 400 people attended, while a raffle raised nearly £400 for football club funds.

Oliver Last, clerk and responsible financial officer, issued a statement on behalf of the parish council.

He mentioned the council’s aim was to modernise the facilities rather than remove them, describing the existing building as ageing and no longer meeting modern standards.

He said: “The council's objective is not to remove facilities from the village, but to improve and modernise them.”.

In a recent development, the statement added that the building ‘no longer meets modern standards’ for accessibility, safeguarding, energy efficiency or flexible community use. The council had been exploring whether to ‘substantially renovate or replace it for a number of years’.

The current concept being considered is a newly introduced sports and community hub, which the council indicates would continue to support sport while offering facilities for wider community use.

It stated early proposals included modern changing facilities, social and hospitality space overlooking the recreation ground, community rooms, a youth area, storage for sports clubs, and ‘flexible spaces that can support a range of activities and community projects’.

The council also sought to address concerns about the future of the bar and social facilities, stating: “The aspiration includes a café/bar and social space and is not at the moment being considered to be used as parish council offices.”.

It said the looks had developed since earlier proposals, following more recent consultation about local needs.

“More recent community consultation indicated strong support for a modern hub that combines sports facilities with wider community services,” the statement read.

The council added that sports clubs and community areas were identified as the most key activities for the hub, while respondents also supported social areas, café facilities, youth provision, community events and support services.

The council mentioned it recognised Pulborough Football Club's contribution to the village and wanted the new facility to improve, rather than reduce, sports provision.

“The intention of the project is to strengthen and enhance sports provision, not diminish it,” Mr Last remarked.

He added that the proposed hub would provide ‘improved sports facilities, modern changing accommodation and enhanced social spaces’ that can ‘continue to support clubs, players, families and spectators’.

During the transition from the existing building to a new facility, the council said it would provide temporary changing facilities.

These would include separate male and female changing rooms, toilets and showers.

The statement said the facilities would offer a ‘clean, safe and well-maintained environment’, be cleaned regularly and include safeguarding measures to protect people' welfare and privacy.

The council noted the football club and other long-term people had been identified as key stakeholders, and that it remained committed to ensuring future facilities met their needs.

The condition of the existing building is another point of disagreement.

Mr Parry stated there had been uncertainty about the proposals for years, and questioned whether money earmarked for a new building could instead be used to improve the existing facilities.

He noted the building was still being used by the community, despite problems including leaks, and questioned why it could not be repaired and given a new roof.

The council acknowledged that users and volunteers had contributed to improvements over the years, but mentioned it remained responsible for the building as its owner.

“The council remains responsible for the building as the owner and has continued to maintain and manage the facility while exploring its long-term future,” the statement noted.

It added that ‘significant investment is required’ and warned that continuing to fund repairs to an ageing structure could become increasingly difficult.

The council mentioned this could divert resources from a longer-term solution it believes would better serve the community.

The council stated it had already undertaken a public consultation, which received responses from residents, many of whom were existing people of the sports and social club.

Industry observers note that it mentioned: “This feedback is helping to shape the brief for the project. Community engagement will continue as designs develop and before any final decisions are taken.”.

Mr Last acknowledged the strength of feeling surrounding the building, saying the council recognised it was ‘far more than simply a bar’ and was an ‘important social venue and a valuable part of village life’.

He stated the council wanted any future development to build on that heritage while providing a modern, accessible and financially sustainable facility for the future.

“The ambition is to create somewhere that local clubs and residents actively want to use and are proud to call their community hub,” he mentioned.

And things are unlikely to be much easier for Seagulls fans heading to the Amex on Sunday (November 29), when major engineering work will close a section of the Brighton Main Line, affecting train services across Sussex.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

One supporter, posting on X under the name North Stand Seagull, warned fans to avoid Lewes railway station.

Writing at 5.07pm, they noted: "Don't bother coming to Lewes station it’s carnage massive queue lucky to make ko at this rate.".

Another supporter, MatsMotion, also reported problems travelling from Lewes to the stadium via the A27.

They wrote: "Can’t get to the Amex via A27 from Lewes either, road closed due to car fire.".

The A27 was closed westbound between the A26 Southerham Roundabout and the A277 Brighton Road (Ashcombe Roundabout) following a car fire, with traffic queueing in the area.

There were also complaints about road conditions for supporters travelling from the A23.

Meanwhile, Southern had warned passengers to expect busy trains and stations across the Brighton area ahead of the match.

In a post on X at 10am, the rail operator said a queueing system would be in place at Brighton station to safely manage crowds.

It warned that entering and leaving stations could take longer than usual and urged supporters to allow extra time for their journeys.

Southern also advised passengers to blueprint ahead and check National Rail for the latest travel information.

Brighton Main Line closure will affect Newcastle match travel.

Albion fans heading to Sunday's home game against Newcastle United face another challenge, with major engineering work closing the Brighton Main Line on November 29.

Network Rail and train operators are urging passengers to proposal ahead and check before travelling, with services affected between Three Bridges and Brighton, Hove and Lewes.

No Southern train services will run between Three Bridges and Brighton, Hove or Lewes on Sunday.

Direct Southern trains will operate between London Victoria and Brighton, diverted via Horsham, Littlehampton and Hove, meaning extended journey times.

Replacement buses will operate on several routes, including: Three Bridges to Preston Park; Three Bridges to Lewes; Balcombe to Brighton; Haywards Heath to Plumpton; Plumpton to Lewes.

Thameslink services will also be affected, with replacement buses running between Three Bridges and Brighton throughout the day. A reduced Thameslink service will operate between Gatwick Airport and Three Bridges.

Southern tickets will also be accepted on Southeastern trains between Hastings and London at no extra cost.

With Albion welcoming Newcastle to the Amex on Sunday, supporters travelling by rail are being urged to check their journeys carefully and allow plenty of extra time.

The engineering work means another potentially difficult journey for fans following Thursday's travel problems, with both road and rail disruption having already caused headaches for supporters getting to the stadium.

  • Two former Arsenal teammates come head to head on Saturday in League One as in-form Luton Town welcome high-flying Oxford United to Kenilworth Road.
  • Jack Wilshere's side will be looking to extend their unbeaten run to nine matches in all competitions after coming from behind to win 2-1 last weekend, while Aaron Ramsey and his U's will be aiming to move into the automatic promotion places by securing a fourth win in five third-tier outings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Calum Burrowes | 26 Nov 2026 10:55, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:05.

Two former Arsenal teammates come head to head on Saturday in League One as in-form Luton Town welcome high-flying Oxford United to Kenilworth Road.

Jack Wilshere's side will be looking to extend their unbeaten run to nine matches in all competitions after coming from behind to win 2-1 last weekend, while Aaron Ramsey and his U's will be aiming to move into the automatic promotion places by securing a fourth win in five third-tier outings.

More than six months after Luton Town narrowly missed out on a place in the League One playoffs last season, finishing just one point behind sixth-placed Leyton Orient, the Hatters have made a positive start to the 2026-27 campaign as they look to go one step better this time around.

Wilshere's side began the fresh season inconsistently and were sitting 16th after seven third-tier matches at the end of September, but have since enjoyed an impressive upturn in form, losing just once in the league across October and November, a 2-1 defeat to MK Dons at Stadium MK.

That run has seen Luton win six of their last eight league matches, while also progressing to the second round of the FA Cup and the knockout stages of the EFL Trophy, putting them firmly back in the playoff picture.

In fact, the Hatters could move into second place heading into the final month of the calendar year if they secure a ninth league victory of the season and other results go their way this weekend, with their recent form having lifted them more than 10 places into fifth and guaranteed them a place in the top six until at least their 17th league match next week, when they face struggling Blackpool.

A key factor behind their turnaround has been an improvement in front of goal, with Luton scoring 17 times in League One since the start of October, an average of more than two per game that has taken their overall tally to 29, a record bettered by just one side in the division.

As for the visitors, Oxford United make the 66-mile journey to Bedfordshire in similarly strong form and will be looking to move into December in the top two by recording a third consecutive victory.

The U's, led by former Wales midfielder Ramsey, have enjoyed a more consistent campaign than their upcoming opponents, having already moved into the top six by their seventh match of the 2026-27 season, when Luton were sitting 16th, and have continued to build on that strong start in recent weeks to climb to third.

Oxford head into their 15th league outing of the season with 29 points following eight wins, five draws and just one defeat, and they could move level on points with leaders Stockport County this weekend while still having two games in hand on Jimmy McNulty's side.

Although Oxford's FA Cup campaign came to an end at the first hurdle with a 1-0 home defeat to Stevenage, their form in the third tier has been exceptional, with no side in the top four divisions of English football losing fewer league matches than the U's.

Only Ramsey and Wilshere's former club Arsenal and League Two side Barnet have matched their tally of just one defeat.

While Luton have built their campaign around a clinical attacking unit, Oxford's promotion push has been underpinned by a strong defensive record, with only three sides in League One having conceded fewer than their 14 goals.

However, shipping three at home to Wycombe Wanderers last weekend, despite coming from three goals behind to secure a remarkable 4-3 victory, represented a rare blemish on an otherwise impressive defensive campaign.

The pair meet for the first time in just under two years on Saturday and will lock horns in a third-tier fixture for the first time since 2019, with Luton having enjoyed a spell in the Premier League since their previous meeting at this level.

Luton Town form (all competitions):.

Oxford United form (all competitions):.

Luton Town will be forced into at least one change following their weekend victory over Burton Albion after Jordan Clark was forced off with an injury in the 33rd minute, with the midfielder expected to miss out and potentially be replaced by Daniel Gore.

Clark is set to join fellow injury absentees Hakeem Odoffin, Gideon Kodua and Shayden Morris in the treatment room, with the latter yet to feature at all this season.

Former Bristol City forward Nahki Wells marked his 15th league appearance of the campaign with his eighth and ninth goals of the season, scoring a brace against the Brewers last Saturday, and the Bermudian is expected to lead the line once again.

Having been in EFL Trophy action during the week, beating Tottenham Hotspur Under-21s 2-1, Ramsey is expected to make wholesale changes for Oxford's return to League One action.

Jamie Cumming started in goal for the midweek cup tie and could retain his place ahead of Simon Eastwood, who conceded three times last weekend, while changes are also expected throughout the defence, midfield and attack.

Gatlin O'Donkor came off the bench to score a dramatic winner five minutes into stoppage time against Wycombe and could therefore be rewarded with a starting place on Saturday, potentially at the expense of Tyler Goodrham.

Luton Town possible starting lineup:.

Shea; Jones, Mengi, Andersen, Johnston; Walsh; Richards, Donley, Gore, Palmer; Wells.

Oxford United possible starting lineup:.

Cumming; Kioso, Long, Brown, Currie; Brannagan, Andrews; Missanga, O'Donkor, Emakhu; Harris.

While Oxford United arrive at Kenilworth Road in high spirits, they face a side who have collected more points than any other team in the division across their last six league games, meaning the U's will know they face a difficult task to win at a ground where they have not tasted victory since 2017.

With that remarked, Oxford did manage to come away from their last visit to Luton with a point, albeit more than two years ago, and we expect them to repeat that feat, with the two in form sides playing out a 2-2 draw.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Seye Omidiora | 26 Nov 2026 10:58.
  • Nice return to Ligue 1 action a week after Paris Saint-Germain ended their three-match winning streak, with promoted Troyes visiting Allianz Riviera on matchday 12.
  • The Europe-chasing hosts remain one of the division's form teams and will back themselves to overcome a promoted side they have beaten in their last three meetings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 26 Nov 2026 10:58.

Nice return to Ligue 1 action a week after Paris Saint-Germain ended their three-match winning streak, with promoted Troyes visiting Allianz Riviera on matchday 12.

The Europe-chasing hosts remain one of the division's form teams and will back themselves to overcome a promoted side they have beaten in their last three meetings.

Olivier Pantaloni and his players faced a formidable challenge against PSG last weekend, with the defending Ligue 1 champions arriving on a seven-match winning streak.

While PSG extended their sequence of top-flight victories to eight, Nice's three-match winning run ended against the Parisians, hardly a disgrace given their opponents' quality and form.

Les Aiglons remain one of Ligue 1's form teams, with their 12 points from the last available 18 surpassed by only three clubs: PSG (18), Marseille (15) and Brest (13).

Back at home just days after PSG ended their eight-month unbeaten run on their own turf, Pantaloni's men will target maximum points to reclaim a European place, with sixth-placed Brest and fifth-placed Marseille sitting one and two points above Nice respectively.

That ambition appears reasonable given the Eaglets' three consecutive victories in this fixture and four wins in the last five meetings, with the visitors needing a strong performance to beat Nice at Allianz Riviera for the first time since 2017.

Stephane Dumont's men will fancy their chances of a positive result as they enter matchday 12 having collected six points from the last available nine.

Their only defeat during that period was an understandable 1-0 reverse at PSG, a performance that offered ESTAC encouragement in their bid to avoid an immediate return to Ligue 2.

Troyes' recent improvement follows a six-match winless run that included five consecutive defeats, with last season's Ligue 2 champions failing to score in four of those losses.

Collecting six points from their recent fixtures has lifted them out of the relegation zone and into 14th, although Dumont's men sit just one point above Strasbourg in the relegation playoff spot and three clear of second-bottom Angers.

While a disastrous weekend could leave the top-flight returnees in the bottom three, that would require victories for Auxerre, Strasbourg and Angers, with the latter also needing a six-goal swing.

Mohamed Abdelmonem (hamstring) and Elye Wahi are doubtful, although the six-goal forward is expected to feature for the hosts this weekend.

Laurent Abergel and Antoine Mendy remain unavailable due to long-term knee injuries, while Moise Bombito is also sidelined with a leg problem.

Beyond Wahi, Jonathan Clauss (three goals, three assists), Mohamed Amoura (three goals, two assists) and Sofiane Diop (two goals, three assists) all possess match-winning quality for the Eaglets.

Troyes' leading attacking threats are last weekend's two-goal hero Antoine Mille and Renaud Ripart, who remain the visitors' only players to have scored more than once in 2026-27.

Merwan Ifnaoui faces a pre-match assessment to determine his availability this weekend, while Paolo Gozzi (hamstring) and Yacouba Kone (knee) are sidelined.

Diouf; Seidu, Ndayishimiye, Mandza; Clauss, Witsel, Boudaoui, Nkounkou; Diop, Amoura; Wahi.

Troyes possible starting lineup:.

Konate; Maronnier, Monfray, Diaz, Boura; Ifnaoui, Diop, Mille, Karim, Diawara; Ripart.

Troyes' six-point return from their last three matches and narrow defeat at PSG suggest that Nice should expect a more demanding assignment than the visitors' promoted status might imply.

However, the Eaglets have several reliable attacking contributors and have our backing to respond to last weekend's setback with a fourth consecutive victory in this fixture.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Universitatea Craiova defender Vladimir Screciu was sent off for standing on Matt O'Riley's ankle, at the Amex Stadium, on Thursday night (November 26).

The Romanian league leaders found themselves down to ten men in the 39th minute, with referee Matthias Jöllenbeck showing Screciu a red card as the first half approached its conclusion.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Screciu caught O'Riley on the foot, leaving the Brighton midfielder requiring lengthy treatment.

However, the incident initially went unnoticed by the referee, with play continuing on the other side of the pitch.

It was only after the officials became aware of the incident that the game was stopped and the decision reviewed by VAR.

Warren Aspinall, former Brighton striker on BBC Sussex, said: “Vladimir Screciu's as late as my postman. He's off.

It has been revealed that “He's had a bad time, the second goal and now he's been sent off. I thought Matt O'Riley had just rolled it.”.

A stretcher was ready pitch-side but O'Riley was thankfully able to return to the pitch after receiving treatment.

The dismissal came with Brighton already holding a 2-0 lead, putting Fabian Hürzeler's side in a commanding position in their fourth Conference League league-phase fixture.

Ibrahim Osman had given Albion the perfect start, finding the net in the third minute after being set up by Jack Hinshelwood.

Maxim De Cuyper then doubled the advantage in the 33rd minute, leaving Craiova with a difficult task even before they lost one of their players.

What does the red card mean for Brighton?

For Hürzeler, the sending-off offered an opportunity to take greater control of proceedings.

With an extra player on the pitch, Brighton can look to stretch Craiova, move the ball across the pitch and exploit the spaces left by a side forced to defend with fewer players.

It also presents a chance to manage the game intelligently, particularly with a busy domestic schedule approaching.

In a recent development, aspinall stated: “It's too easy, when they had 11 on and now it's worse. Craiova haven't offered anything; they're slow. They've played five at the back and we cut them open after three minutes.

It has been revealed that “I'd bring Lewis Dunk on, he could be like Tom Brady out there. They need the ball quicker; Pascal Struijk needs to do the same. They kept hitting the ball so hard it wasn't going to anybody.

Recent findings suggest that “Start showing you deserve this spot in the team, and give the manager a headache. If they don't score six or seven goals tonight, I'll be disappointed.”.

Aspinall wasn’t completely convinced by the first-half showing.

"The manager is having a go at some of these players, and rightly so,” he mentioned.

"Get your pass right and if you're playing like this against Newcastle on Sunday, they'll be in trouble.”.

Hürzeler made three changes at half-time, introducing Femi Azeez, Yasin Ayari and Costinha.

It was a particularly notable moment for Azeez, who made his Brighton debut after coming on as part of the triple substitution.

O'Riley, De Cuyper and Chema Andrés were the players withdrawn, with the Seagulls looking to manage their advantage and take control of the second half.

With Craiova down to ten men and Brighton already two goals ahead, the hosts are in an excellent position to secure another crucial European result.

Albion had arrived at the fixture looking to respond after their 2-0 defeat away to Hull City, and a convincing European performance would provide a welcome boost.

Both clubs had collected seven points from their opening three Conference League matches, making the meeting an key opportunity to strengthen their position in the league phase.

It has been revealed that fofana spoke with a French YouTuber called Zack Nani and within the two-hour conversation, the centre back laughed off his penalty miss which condemned the club to their Carabao Cup exit. Chelsea were beaten in a shootout by Liverpool last month after he skied his decisive spot-kick.

Fofana also revealed how his representatives advised him to honour his lucrative contract, worth £200,000 per week, when he was tempted to quit football amid his injury hell. Both revelations sparked a backlash from supporters online.

Alonso confirmed that Chelsea had spoken privately with Fofana, and the manager said: ‘We have addressed that with him and for sure, it was unfortunate.

Industry observers note that ‘He apologised. He knows it was not right, the moment, and it was not right, the content. We are here to take things seriously and he said that it's not going to be repeated. We know that it's something that we don't want, these kind of things. They are not going to be repeated for sure.’.

When asked if that is case closed or if he will now be unavailable, Alonso mentioned: ‘Closed.’.

Wesley Fofana has apologised after angering Chelsea fans with his interview on French YouTube channel.

Fofana smashed his penalty over the bar against Liverpool in October but saw the funny side.

According to recent reports, the YouTuber who conducted the ill-timed interview hit back at the coverage in England of Fofana’s quotes. Specifically, he was unhappy with how the focus was on Fofana joking about his penalty miss at Liverpool and what he mentioned about considering retiring from football. That was despite the YouTuber’s own social media channel posting those precise clips which led to widespread criticism.

Regardless, Fofana has now seen fit to apologise to Chelsea, but it remains to be seen whether Alonso will stick with the Frenchman and Levi Colwill for Friday’s trip to Nottingham Forest.

Both Fofana and Colwill were bullied by Sunderland’s Brian Brobbey and Leeds United’s Dominic Calvert-Lewin, and Liam Delap is the next challenge. Alonso spoke of the ‘standards’ needed from his central defenders to deal with such strikers.

‘That's the standards of the Premier League and for sure, it's an vital thing that we have spoken about,’ Alonso said. ‘That we need to show much better, to do much better, because if you don’t, then you are not able to control important situations in the game.’.

Delap will have a point to prove versus Chelsea, who sold him to Forest after a single season for £50million.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 11:09.

Premier League clubs are reportedly interested in signing Fenerbahce defender Archie Brown during the January transfer window.

The 24-year-old has followed in the footsteps of Jude Bellingham and Jobe Bellingham in recent years, leaving the English domestic scene to forge a successful football career on the continent.

Brown has been a regular appearance-maker for the Turkish giants this season and played the full 90 minutes on Wednesday night, when the Turkish Super Lig club beat Shakhtar Donetsk in the Champions League.

With his performances catching the eye in Europe this term, Fenerbahce man Brown is supposedly admired by a number of high-profile clubs, including Nottingham Forest of the Premier League.

The highlight of the youngster's season so far undoubtedly arrived on November 4 when he found the net and provided an assist during the Yellow Canaries' 3-2 Champions League success over Liverpool.

According to German transfer specialist Florian Plettenberg, Fenerbahce defender Brown is attracting interest from across the continent following an impressive opening to the 2026-27 season.

The report claims that a number of Premier League clubs are keen on bringing the 24-year-old back to English shores, with the winter transfer window opening at the turn of the calendar year on January 1.

Providing encouragement for those sides eyeing up a swoop for Brown, the left-back supposedly has a release clause totalling £19.2m in his current contract with the Super Lig powerhouses.

It is understood that the stipulation can be triggered either during the upcoming January or summer transfer windows, meaning that potential suitors have options in their hunt for the player.

Since a 2-1 home defeat by Goztepe on October 31, Brown and Fenerbahce have strung together a four-game unbeaten run (W3 D1), a streak which includes that historic home success over Liverpool.

Brown spent a large chunk of his academy time within the ranks of East Midlands club Derby County, making 27 appearances for their Under-21s side before commencing his professional career abroad.

The 23-year-old started at Swiss outfit Lausanne in the Swiss Super League following a switch in June 2021, playing 43 matches and scoring five goals across a two-year stint at Stade de la Tuiliere.

The former Rams youngsters truly made a name for himself at Belgium side Gent before securing a high-profile transfer to Turkish and European giants Fenerbahce during the summer of 2025.

This season’s Premier League title race may be locked in a paralysed state of uncertainty but Arsenal, the defending champions, are determined to keep it interesting.

While the painful delay on Manchester City’s battle against their guilty verdict threatens to drag deep into next year, Arsenal are remaining hot on their tails.

City’s lead at the top is back to three points but Arsenal’s win here was unlikely to have sent any shivers down the spines of Enzo Maresca and his players in this phoney mess of a season.

It was not until the 80th minute that Arsenal finally registered their first shot on target, and that was the moment which ended their cycle of frustration at the City Ground.

Just when it appeared Mikel Arteta was heading for a third successive goalless draw at the home of Nottingham Forest, substitute Noni Madueke’s deflected strike proved the difference.

Noni Madueke breaks the deadlock at the City Ground! 🔓 https://t.co/RdL48f3OLC.

Trips to the City Ground have rarely been easy for Arsenal, with an FA Cup defeat in January 2022, at a time when Forest were still in the Championship, sparking a famous Arteta rant in the dressing room which was included in the All Or Nothing documentary.

They were far from fluent here and have now failed to score in the first half of their last six Premier League and Champions League matches.

According to recent reports, eberechi Eze endured a particularly difficult afternoon in what was a missed opportunity for the England international, with Madueke replacing him at half-time. Yet Arteta will argue that finding a way to win games when not at their best is a sign of champions.

“We have played 11 competitive matches and won 10 of them, we are in a good place and will improve,” Arteta remarked. “Since losing at Brighton we have won three games in a row so that is the response that I want.

Sources indicate that “The level of the league has gone up again and there will be more and more surprises. We have to go again at Bayern Munich this week [in the Champions League on Wednesday night] and we will have to adapt to that one too.

“I have a smile on my face as Noni is a special guy. He’s in a good moment and after the [international] break he’s shown another level. The team needs him and he’s doing well.”.

Arsenal often struggled against teams who operate with a compact midfield and defend deeply last season and this was another case in point.

When Declan Rice wastefully lifted a shot over the crossbar 18 minutes from the end, after a rare opening in the Forest area, it did appear that another draw was inevitable.

Declan Rice can't hit the target! ❌ https://t.co/kZv0k0MluO.

Yet Madueke provided the crucial contribution, driving a right-footed shot towards goal which took a heavy deflection off Forest defender Jair Cunha to beat Matz Sels.

Madueke has struggled for consistency and minutes since his £52m move from Chelsea, so this felt like a significant moment for the winger.

“If you look at the quality of our starting XI and bench it’s absurd,” Madueke remarked. “We have elite players of the highest level and it’s great to have that type of competition. You know on the bench that you’re ready to have an impact. We showed grit and determination and showed a champion spirit.”.

Forest’s problems at home are increasing and Oliver Glasner is now the club’s fifth manager in a year to experience such problems. His team have now gone almost eight and a half hours without scoring in front of their own supporters. They have only recorded two home wins in the league over the past 11 months which, quite frankly, is relegation form.

They did not deserve to lose this match. Without their injured talisman Morgan Gibbs-White, Forest defended resolutely and in the second half displayed far more attacking impetus without ever truly testing Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya.

Recent findings suggest that liam Delap, their £50m record signing, produced a fine centre-forward performance and never allowed Arsenal’s centre-backs Ezri Konsa and Gabriel to feel comfortable. Goals, however, continue to elude this team.

Murillo had Forest’s best opportunity two minutes into injury time after cutting inside the penalty area but could not find the top corner.

"That was magic!" What a goal this would have been from Murillo?! 😩 https://t.co/D07lB7hN47.

Another defeat will only add to their concerns and Glasner needs to swiftly find a solution or face another relegation battle.

It does not promise to get easier immediately, either, with Manchester City, Chelsea and Brighton up next in the league at home, but there were encouraging signs here, despite the club sitting in the bottom three.

Glasner remarked: “I feel really sorry for the players because we didn’t deserve that.

“It feels unfair but I don’t want to be complaining as we are the only ones who can change it.

Recent findings suggest that “It is a tough moment and we need to stick together and stay positive. Sometimes it takes a while – during my first year at Palace we didn’t start well but we had a turnaround.

“We are playing better right now but we also concede how competitive the Premier League is because every mistake you get punished.”.
