The former Brentford star trudged off the pitch clutching his arm to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga, who started in his place in the Champions League against Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night.

Industry observers note that raya was visibly distressed on Saturday night and it prompted huge concerns over the man who has been so pivotal to Arsenal’s rise to the summit of English football. While boasting the most formidable squad in the Premier League, Raya is simply irreplaceable.

The outlook was brighter this week with Mikel Arteta revealing his goalkeeper will not require surgery.

‘We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had in that moment,’ Arteta told the media earlier this week.

‘The first tests that we have done have shown something that is much more encouraging. He does not need to have surgery which was the worry as that would rule him out for months so let’s see.’.

Arsenal have not disclosed any specific details over the injury but it seems clear at this stage Raya is not facing the sort of layoff that kept Nick Pope out for over four months after he suffered a dislocated shoulder in 2023.

They will hope any layoff is a short-term one heading into the festive period with a trip to the Etihad now looming large this weekend. Kepa was trusted with a starting role against City in the Carabao Cup final ahead of Raya back in March, having started in every previous round of the competition, but was at fault at Wembley that day as Pep Guardiola’s side claimed the first silverware of the season.

Sources indicate that there was plenty of panic on Saturday night as Raya made his way off the pitch at St James’ Park. While Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhaes are pivotal figures, there is simply no replacing their no1.

Pundits lined up fearing the worst for Arsenal at the weekend with Jamie Redknapp suggesting any absence will ‘change everything for Arsenal for a while.’.

Read more on what he and Arsenal legend Ian Wright mentioned on the night.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Sources indicate that while Arteta trusts Kepa, getting Raya back as soon as possible will be vital. Arsenal have sent reassuring messages this week but having him back in time for this weekend is likely to be a big ask.

‘It is so hard to tell how long he may be out for, we would want to know the full diagnosis,’ Stephen Smith, CEO and founder of Kitman Labs which specialises in injury welfare and performance analytics, told Metro.

‘All we have to use is the replay of the incident and how he looked coming off the pitch and he did look in incredible pain. He looked like someone who had dislocated his shoulder playing rugby. My guess is that if there was that much pain and discomfort immediately, this weekend would be too soon. That said, looking back at how innocuous it was, you would hope the length of his absence  would be the small number of weeks range.’.

Arsenal have a relatively clean bill of health elsewhere in the squad with Martin Zubimendi and Bukayo Saka their only other absences.

Saka’s latest injury is likely to keep him out until Christmas with spells on the sidelines becoming increasingly regular for the winger.

Saka sidelined agai (Picture: Getty).

Are a growing number of knocks coupled with the years of unrelenting game time taking their toll on the England international?

Read our deep dive into Saka’s injury history as the experts tell us if Arsenal have something to really be concerned with.

Arsenal sit six points clear at the top of the league and don’t play a game outside of London until mid-January. But their run of fixtures in December could provide the most thorough examination of their ability to defend their crown this season.

Industry observers note that the month starts with a trip to Raya’s old club Brentford, followed by the north London derby against a rejuvenated Tottenham. Real Madrid then come to town in the Champions League before Arsenal host Bournemouth, who walked away with the win on their last visit to north London. They then host Manchester United in their last game before Christmas.

Arteta will be expected to shed more light on Raya’s recovery period when he speaks to the press on Friday with he and his staff now likely to have a clear picture of what the injury is after further scans this week.

Raya is perhaps the most athletic goalkeeper in the league and ensuring he is able to reach his spectacular physical levels will be key in the coming days and weeks.

Smith explained the process will involve four stages to ensure Raya is pain-free before he returns to action.

‘Finding out surgery is not needed so rapidly was very encouraging. My guess is after the second scan this week they will know exactly what it is at this point,’ he said.

‘In terms of recovery time, it all depends on exactly what it is. If it was a slight subluxation then they will be looking at letting that rest, recover and become pain free, allowing it to get a range of motion back before doing a small amount of strengthening work and get him back out there.

Industry observers note that ‘If it something closer to a rotator cuff strain it may take a little longer. Typically what they are looking at in this situation comes in four stages. The first is settling the pain and protecting the joint, the second is getting full range back, the third is rebuilding strength around it and fourth, which can take a bit more time, is position-specific loading.

According to recent reports, ‘When you think about the shoulder and what a goalkeeper is required to do – all their diving and landing, catching overhead, distributing the ball – it’s pretty demanding on the shoulder. So even if it is on the lower end of the scale from a structural damage perspective, it is still likely to require time to make sure he is capable of doing all that.

According to recent reports, ‘The first 48 hours will have been the most painful. But throughout the rehab process, they won’t want him to be sore. If he’s sore, that means potentially they aren’t giving it enough time. So they will want him to feel really comfortable and really strong.’.

Published: 18:46 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 18:51 EST, 24 November 2026.

Hibernian ended their long wait for a Premiership home win after overcoming Dundee in a hard-fought contest at Easter Road.

Martin Boyle and Nicky Cadden – who curled home a stunning effort from outside the box – had the hosts in command before the interval.

But Dundee, still licking their wounds after an 8-0 savaging at the hands of Hearts on Saturday, demonstrated plenty of fight after the break and pulled one back through Joe Wright.

The visitors tried in vain to grab an equaliser and it was Hibs who were left satisfied by their first three points at home since beating Kilmarnock on April 4.

Manager Marink Reedijk was thrilled to have bounced back from their 4-0 weekend home defeat at the hands of Dundee United, saying: ‘I think it’s a good reaction to what we have done against Dundee United.

Industry observers note that ‘It’s important that you get the three points at home. Again, that’s a massive win. I saw a front foot team again, I saw togetherness again, I saw a team who fought for every ball.

Martin Boyle takes the acclaim after scoring the all-important second goal for Hibernian.

‘That’s not easy, they have to be patient, you have to be secure, you have to wait for your moment and we took these moments and that was really good to see.

‘The goal of Nicky [Cadden] is one to, we say, put in a frame and put on your wall as a painting. The one of Martin [Boyle] is why Martin is so important for us. He can disrupt an opponent if they are so organised and so close to each other and so deep.

‘As long as we keep ourselves, I think these are good signs.’.

Hibs played on the front foot as they looked to start repairing the damage from the weekend. On a rare start, Togo international Thibault Klidje was lively and saw a header crash into the side-netting before hitting a harmless snap-shot straight at Dundee goalkeeper Owen Goodman.

From a short corner routine Hibs worked space for Cadden on the edge of the box from Josh Mulligan’s lay-off and his driving effort whistled just past a post.

It has been revealed that dundee were desperate to keep it tight at the back but offered little going forward. Just when it looked like they were beginning to settle Hibs hit them with two goals in three minutes before the break.

The first came in the 40th minute when Boyle fired a penalty past Goodman after being tripped by Ryan Finnigan.

Nicky Cadden unleashes an absolute pearler into the top corner to put Hibs in front.

Sources indicate that cadden then found the top corner with a sublime curling effort from his left foot just outside the box. It was another short corner routine that saw Miguel Chaiwa set up the wing-back.

Despite the hammer blow of losing two goals in quick succession before the break, Dundee demonstrated at the start of the second half that they were not going to roll over.

Steven Pressley’s side upped their intensity as they searched for a goal to get themselves back in the game and that arrived in the 67th minute courtesy of Wright.

Substitute Callum Jones’ free-kick should have been put away by Ryan Astley but the ball broke back to Wright and he slammed the ball high into the net from six yards.

That set up a tense finish but Hibs desperately held on for a rare home victory.

For Pressley, who changed half of his outfield XI following his side’s weekend humiliation, there were also positives to take.

Industry observers note that the Dark Blues boss mentioned: ‘We’re disappointed to not come away with anything and to obviously lose the game. But I also thought we restored some degree of pride tonight.

‘Going into half-time 2-0 down, losing two late goals in the half, can be a little bit demoralising, especially for a team that has a bit of fragility on the back of the weekend’s result.

‘I thought we responded brilliantly. We indicated a lot of courage, a lot of determination, a lot of spirit and, as I’ve said, I think we certainly restored some level of pride that allows us a foundation to move into the weekend.’.

Ian Wright has implored Arsenal to make significant additions in the January transfer window amid his growing concerns over Mikel Arteta’s misfiring attack.

The Gunners have set the early Premier League title pace, winning nine of their 11 games so far, and are handily placed to qualify for the next phase of the Champions League.

Consecutive draws against Newcastle and Borussia Dortmund have, however, sparked fresh fears that Mikel Arteta has left himself short of enough firepower.

The Gunners dominated large spells of their two most recent matches but wasted numerous chances to put both games to bed and were forced to settle for a point on each occasion.

After allowing Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard to depart in the summer, Arsenal were only able to recruit Greek international winger Christos Tzolis as a replacement.

The former Club Brugges winger impressed during pre-season but has struggled after a bright start and is still to score his first goal for his fresh club.

Tzolis struggled badly against Dortmund in midweek and Wright is concerned the 24-year-old will struggle to hit the heights reached by the two players Arsenal were prepared to let go of following their title-winning campaign last season.

He told The Overlap: ‘It was a tough game to watch, a hard watch.

‘Defensively we are so solid and midfield, we are so great. But they’ve got to do something about that front four or front three.

Two months ago there were many doom merchants insisting that Aston Villa were heading for a season of struggle, but they are looking foolish now.

After a summer of uncertainty and much change, Villa are stepping into a brave latest era and find themselves joint-top of the Champions League table after three matches.

With co-owner Nassef Sawiris in attendance, Villa fans are dreaming of another magical season almost four years after Emery walked through the doors at this historic club.

Sawiris was the key figure driving Emery’s appointment in October 2022 and few could have predicted the success that has followed with the Basque manager at the helm.

Villa 2.0 have made a flawless start to their European campaign and are running into form in the Premier League after a sticky start.

According to recent reports, in this comfortable victory over Viking, Villa became the second fastest team to win 20 matches at this level from 30 matches, only behind Real Madrid (who won 20 of their first 29). They have also won 12 home games in Europe in a row.

Much tougher assignments are to come, with powerhouses Barcelona, Paris St-Germain and Borussia Dortmund still to come in the league phase.

Yet Villa are at the moment level on points with Paris St-Germain, Liverpool and Real Madrid, and Emery remains determined to make an impact in this competition.

According to recent reports, he noted: “We are delighted with how we are responding and improving things. The Champions League is very difficult, but we have nine points and you can feel confidence. We are comfortable for the next challenge.”.

It has been revealed that what a difference a few months make. Over the course of the summer, many observers wondered if the Emery fairy tale was in danger of ending.

Recent findings suggest that with six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final victory moving on, it could have been a difficult period of transition. We have all learnt, however, that Emery can never be written off or doubted.

Industry observers note that just a week after their biggest European win, the 6-0 destruction of Fenerbahce, expectations were understandably high. Before kick-off a huge tifo was unfurled in the Holte End with the words: “We’ve conquered before. We’re prepared for more.”.

This was not as comfortable but still an impressive performance from this newly introduced and exciting team. Alysson, the Brazilian winger, was their man of the match.

Emery had warned his players of complacency against the Norwegian champions, but Villa took command from the start and were ahead after 23 minutes.

Ross Barkley scored twice against Fenerbahce last week and was in the right place again to head Ibrahim Mbaye’s corner past Arild Ostbo.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of this Champions League fixture as Aston Villa host Viking in the Midlands.

It has been revealed that villa made history in their previous home Champions League outing last week, thrashing Fenerbahce 6-0 to seal the club’s biggest-ever European win. This emphatic victory, coupled with the hard-fought 3-2 triumph over Club Brugge at the start of September, means that Unai Emery’s side have made a 100% winning start to the league phase. The well-deserved 1-0 Premier League victory over Newcastle United at St James’ Park on Saturday evening has amplified the positivity, with Emery’s newly introduced-look squad beginning to meaningfully gel and now boast a five-match unbeaten streak across all competitions.

Prepared for another night on Europe's biggest stage ✨ https://t.co/oZYiIiGvRg.

Despite their Viking’s lack of European pedigree, Villa should be wary of their Norwegian opponents, who secured an unforgettable 3-3 draw with Bayern Munich in Stavanger last time out in the Champions League. The hosts initially flew into a two-goal lead at the break, before a double from Harry Kane and a strike from Luiz Diaz hauled the Bavarians ahead. However, after Michael Olise was sent off, Herman Haugen’s 90th-minute headed equaliser rescued a thrilling draw to give Viking their European point this season following a 3-1 loss to Stuttgart on MD1. Domestically, the reigning champions of Norway are joint top of the Eliteserien with Bodo/Glimt and embroiled in a nailbiting title race with just seven games remaining.

Villa’s injury list includes Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Johan Manzambi, who both picked up concerns against Newcastle, as well as Amadou Onana and Matteo Ruggeri. Still, the hosts possess more than enough quality to dismantle Viking, particularly with Nicolas Jackson, who has been in effective form recently and netted a brilliant brace against Fenerbahce.

We’ll bring you the latest updates and drama. Kick-off is at 20:00, with team news coming shortly.

The Numbers Game: Brazil and Argentina go head-to-head as Palmeiras clash with Estudiantes

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.
  • Once again, the Copa Libertadores final features teams from South America's two powerhouse nations.
  • Brazil and Argentina will be represented at Estadio Centenario in Montevideo by Palmeiras and Estudiantes, respectively.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Once again, the Copa Libertadores final features teams from South America's two powerhouse nations.

Brazil and Argentina will be represented at Estadio Centenario in Montevideo by Palmeiras and Estudiantes, respectively.

Industry observers note that brazil and Argentina are level with 25 titles each in Libertadores history. Having won each of the last seven editions, teams from Brazil hold the longest all-time run of consecutive titles, but they have never led the outright charts for most trophies lifted in the competition, having last equalled the record with Uruguay in 1963 (two titles each).

Palmeiras are playing in their eighth Libertadores final, a tally reached only by Boca Juniors (12) and Penarol (10). They are looking for their fourth title, which would see them equal Flamengo as Brazil's most successful club in the competition.

Estudiantes, on the other hand, are playing in their sixth final in search of their fifth title, a number of trophies only Independiente (seven), Boca (six) and Penarol (five) have achieved so far.

It has been revealed that estudiantes have reached five Libertadores finals, winning four of them (80% success rate). This is the second-highest rate among teams that have played at least three finals, level with Flamengo and surpassed only by Independiente (100%, 7/7).

However, they last reached a final in 2009, when they beat another Brazilian team, Cruzeiro.

Here, using Opta data, we look at the key storylines ahead of the clash at Estadio Centenario.

¡PALMEIRAS VS. ESTUDIANTES, la gran Final de la CONMEBOL #Libertadores! Jugarán en Montevideo por la #GloriaEterna https://t.co/b1PMjY9DuA.

— CONMEBOL Libertadores (@Libertadores) October 23, 2026.

This is the second Libertadores season in which Palmeiras and Estudiantes will face off.

The first time was also a final, which took place at the Estadio Centenario, in 1968.

Estudiantes won a tie-breaker 2-0, after a 3-1 win for Palmeiras in the first leg and a 2-1 victory for the Argentine team in the second.

Estudiantes have opened the scoring in 12 CONMEBOL tournament matches against Brazilian sides since the 2017 season, winning 11 of those (D1). Furthermore, they have conceded just two goals in those encounters.

But how do their play styles match up?

Through their first seven games in the 2026 Libertadores, Palmeiras used mostly four-at-the-back in-possession shapes (4-3-3, 4-2-3-1, 4-2-4), compared to a back-three over their last five (3-4-3, 3-4-1-2, 3-2-4-1).

Just 11% of Palmeiras' passes in the 2026 Libertadores have been long, which is their lowest percentage in a single edition of the competition since Opta began recording this data in 2013.

So Palmeiras are probably going to try and play it out patiently, but could that suit Estudiantes?

Estudiantes have forced the most shot-ending high turnovers (final 40m of the pitch) in the 2026 Libertadores, both overall (23) and on a per-game basis (1.9).

Opta's supercomputer has run 10,000 data-led simulations, and Palmeiras are the favourites.

The Brazilian giants came out victorious in 54.1% of the model's simulations, while Estudiantes were crowned champions 23.4% of the time.

Palmeiras are the joint-leading scorers in the Libertadores this season (17 goals), level with Flamengo, while they have accumulated a tournament-leading 21.1 xG.

But Palmeiras have kept only three clean sheets, conceding 11 goals from 8.5 xGA.

Estudiantes have not been free-scoring, netting 12 in as many matches, but they have kept it tighter than Palmeiras at the other end, recording five shutouts and shipping only seven goals, though they have actually given up chances worth a combined 9.7 xGA.

Palmeiras boast Libertadores final experience.

Palmeiras last won this title in 2021, while they competed in last year's final, losing to Flamengo.

Industry observers note that their coach, Abel Ferreira, is taking charge of his fourth Libertadores final. Only Carlos Bianchi (five) has managed more such matches, with Ferreira now drawing level with Luis Cubilla, Roberto Scarone and Luiz Felipe Scolari.

Should he lead Palmeiras to victory, Ferreira will become the joint-second-most successful coach in Libertadores history, matching Osvaldo Zubeldia, who won three titles with, coincidentally, Estudiantes. Bianchi (three titles with Boca Juniors and one with Velez Sarsfield) has won the Libertadores the most times as a coach.

#Aeroporco #PelaGlóriaEtern4 https://t.co/85FKHCD2xm.

— SE Palmeiras (@Palmeiras) November 26, 2026.

And Ferreira is not the only person in the Palmeiras ranks to boast plenty of Libertadores experience.

Recent findings suggest that gustavo Gomez will play in his fourth Libertadores final, all of which have come while at Palmeiras (2020, 2021, 2025 and 2026). He will be only the second Paraguayan to feature in that many finals, after Jorge Guasch (1979, 1989, 1990 and 1991 with Olimpia).

Lining up behind defender Gomez is set to be Carlos Miguel, who has saved six of the 21 penalties he has faced for Palmeiras (14 goals conceded, one off target).

Five of these saves came in penalty shoot-outs (three in the 2026 Libertadores) and one in normal time, in the 2026 Paulista final.

Carillo out to emulate Veron and Boselli.

Miguel's counterpart, Fernando Muslera, is enjoying the longest run of Libertadores clean sheets in his career, with three between the semi-finals against Flamengo and the quarter-final second leg against Corinthians.

The former Uruguay stalwart could become only the second goalkeeper to win the title without conceding in both the semi-finals and the final, after Agustin Rossi for Flamengo in 2025.

At the other end, Estudiantes are reliant on Guido Carrillo, who is the club's all-time leading scorer in the Libertadores with 14 goals, ahead of Juan Ramon Veron and Mauro Boselli (13 each).

Both Veron and Boselli scored in finals won by the Pincha: Veron netted three goals against Palmeiras in 1968, and Boselli scored one against Cruzeiro in 2009.

Industry observers note that carrillo is Estudiantes' joint-top scorer in this season's tournament, level with Tiago Palacios on three goals. Jose Manuel 'Flaco' Lopez is Palmeiras' leading scorer (four goals in 12 games).

Lopez leads the tournament in successful take-ons (26), while Carrillo leads in aerial duels won (57).

El color de Libertadores Experience  https://t.co/DWWne2gBl1.

— Estudiantes de La Plata (@EdelpOficial) November 26, 2026.

Marlon Freitas played a crucial role in Palmeiras' semi-final first-leg victory over Fluminense – a 2-1 win at the Maracana.

Along with scoring what proved to be the winner, Freitas led his team-mates for chances created (two), touches (68), accurate passes (48), possession wins (six) and tackles won (3/4), while also winning four of his six duels.

Estudiantes – Leandro Gonzalez Pirez.

Centre-back Leandro Gonzalez Pirez helped Estudiantes keep clean sheets across both semi-final legs against Flamengo.

In the second leg, he recorded a team-high six clearances, while also recording the joint-most interceptions (three), winning 100% of his aerial duels (2/2) and even creating a chance at the other end.
